agent: Claude Code (CLAUDE.md, this repository) — WP-03a verification: item (i) loop_budget default disagreement
summary_for_principal:
This closes another item from the checklist a past session flagged but never confirmed.

A process can declare its own default limit on how many times a loop is allowed to repeat, instead of relying on the system-wide default of 10. The tool that explains a process to a person already reported this correctly. The engine that actually runs the process did not: it silently ignored the process's own choice and always used the system-wide default of 10 instead. So a process author who set a lower limit (say, 2) to catch a loop going wrong would have seen it allowed to run 10 times before anything stopped it.

Fixed so the engine now honors the process's own declared limit, matching what it was already being told. Two tests prove it (one for each of the two places this loop check happens).

Full test suite: 358 passed, 2 new.

Numbered actions:
1. Nothing needs deciding right now.
2. Five checklist items remain — continuing through them next unless you'd rather reprioritize.

Fix what is real, tests first, one PR per verified item.

decisions.headline: D28 — _advance_route and _advance_gate now pass the process's own defaults.loop_budget to check_loop_budget, not a hardcoded None.
decisions.problem: Both engine call sites hardcoded process_default_budget=None, so a loop with no budget of its own always fell through to the format default (10) even when the process declared a different defaults.loop_budget — disagreeing with explain (cli.py), which already implemented the correct 3-tier fallback (loop.budget, else process defaults, else format default).
decisions.cost_to_change: Trivial — an additive parameter on _advance_route and a one-line value change at each of two call sites; no schema or durable-record change.

evidence.source: tests/engine/test_run.py::test_gate_deny_loop_with_no_own_budget_uses_the_process_declared_default, run against the unfixed engine, this session.
